item.title: Hurricane Polo fuels fears of landslides in Mexico as Nolo closes in on Hawaii
item.description: Southwestern Mexico braced for heavy rain and mudslides after Polo became a major hurricane. Forecasters warned another system headed for Hawaii could cause catastrophic flooding later in the week.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: Is Nepal's flood a harbinger of what's to come in the Himalayas?
item.description: Building dams and hydropower plants in the Himalayas holds great promise for providing electricity. In the wake of the Nepal disaster, experts are asking about the risks of such construction.

item.title: Category 5 Hurricane Polo is 'one of the strongest storms ever'
item.description: Hurricane Polo has grown into one of the most powerful Pacific cyclones in decades, and it was expected to skirt Mexico's southwestern coast as a Category 5 storm.

item.title: This farm raised thousands of pigs for slaughter. Now it's growing mushrooms instead
item.description: The U.S. gets nearly a third of its pork from Iowa. One family is making the switch from pigs to more sustainable specialty mushrooms and trying to show other pig farmers how they did it.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: They lost their beachfront house to rising sea levels. The debris are still out there
item.description: When a flood or hurricane destroys a home, it spreads bits of debris for miles. In coastal areas with strong waves and currents, it's almost impossible to pick up all the pieces.

item.title: Archaeologists are racing to save precious artifacts in Alaska after last year's storm
item.description: Last year, remnants of a typhoon damaged homes, infrastructure and an archaeological dig site. Now, archaeologists are trying to get as many objects out as possible before the next storm.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: Will even one of the U.N.'s 17 'sustainable development goals' be met by 2030?
item.description: The 17 goals agreed upon by world leaders are incredibly ambitious. Are we even close to achieving any of them? If we don't, is the project a failure?

item.title: People's houses are collapsing into the ocean. FEMA gives them no other option
item.description: Waterfront homes are collapsing along the coast. Homeowners generally have plenty of warning before their house buckles. So why aren't most houses removed, or at least emptied, before they fall?

item.title: In Florida, textbook publishers are minimizing or removing climate change coverage
item.description: The words "climate change" are slowly being removed from textbooks in Florida and from the state's education standards.
